searches.name: Public Landsat Level 1 availability
searches.result: Planetary Computer landsat-c2-l1 returned zero scenes for this date and area. Its collection is historical MSS rather than Landsat 8 OLI. Use available C2 L2 only as a qualitative visual composite, not as input to a Level 1 active-fire algorithm.

searches.name: east-river
searches.visual_observation: Pale smoke across natural color; SWIR reveals bright pink linear edges west of the large river. Plausible active burning, but diffuse and less visually clear than the later west-river region.

searches.name: north-fields
searches.visual_observation: Bright pink edges are visible through haze, but substantial white cloud and smoke obscure natural-color context. Less suitable for a clearly communicated demonstration.

searches.name: west-river
searches.visual_observation: A coherent bright pink/orange front appears near 113.927E, 3.025S, beside agricultural grids, with a pale natural-color plume extending westward. This is more interpretable active-burning context than NBR change.
searches.crop_reason: Show the bright front and its immediate smoke context in the same geographic window. Crop selected after imagery inspection, not an unbiased sample.
searches.same_date_result: Aqua 2, S-NPP 27, Terra 4, NOAA-20 51 confidence-filtered observations in the crop. Closest pass is NOAA-20 06:22 UTC (16 points), 227.16 minutes after Landsat. Zero observations meet the predefined +/-60-minute rule. No window was widened.

reviewer: AI-assisted visual review, non-blinded; no external expert or practitioner validation
interpretation: Corroboration is limited to burning at this place and UTC date. The independent instrument and NASA-documented scene support that interpretation; later FIRMS passes are neither simultaneous nor individual-pixel truth.
